page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-180-lssd is a general-purpose, high-density compute instance configured with an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 180 vCPUs across 90 dedicated physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system incorporates 720 GB of system memory, matching a standard 4:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Attached storage includes 6,432 GB of local NVMe SSDs arranged across 16 units, providing high-bandwidth local input/output capability directly bound to the hardware configuration. No discrete GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate top-tier performance in parallel execution environments. The instance scores 22,071.0 in Geekbench multi-core tests and 277,289.81 in multi-core stress-ng benchmarks, placing both in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems. Instruction-specific capabilities are reinforced by hardware support for AVX-512 extensions, yielding strong PassMark CPU extended instruction and encryption ratings. Memory subsystem benchmarks show high uncached bandwidth, reaching 345.79 GB/s for read operations and 167.45 GB/s for writes. Single-core performance remains solid, marked by a Geekbench single-core score of 2,021.0.

Application-level measurements indicate extreme efficiency in in-memory processing and parallel input/output. The platform achieved 211.54 million operations per second in Redis SET operations alongside top-tier static web throughput of 94.32 GB/s. For CPU-based machine learning inference, prompt processing reaches 5,249.66 tokens per second on small models and 326.47 tokens per second on 7B models. From a qualitative cost-efficiency standpoint, the dense aggregation of 180 dedicated vCPUs with 6,432 GB of integrated high-speed NVMe storage provides high compute density, though workloads that do not exploit its localized NVMe storage or massive thread parallelism will underutilize its allocated resources.

This instance configuration is suited for scale-out distributed databases, high-throughput in-memory caching tiers, intensive compilation suites, static web serving infrastructure, and large-scale data transformation (ETL) pipelines.
